Credit Recovery
Decision Copilot

One AI agent copies a bankruptcy liquidation table with a cited source row for every number. Deterministic code recomputes the creditor waterfall, checks it against the debtor's filing, and lets an analyst stress the assumptions.

Tuğrul Özsoy · October 26, 2026
github.com/tugrul-ozsoy/credit-recovery-copilot

Why I built this

Liquidation value is not asset value minus a haircut

  • Preparing for the UCLA Credit Pitch Competition, I had to understand liquidation recovery in a distressed credit.
  • Recovery depends on asset-specific haircuts, secured vs unsecured claims, collateral and guarantees, legal-entity boundaries, administration costs and the order of payment.
  • A model can look reasonable, add up, and still mislead if the waterfall or structure is wrong.

Could this fragile, manual analysis become reproducible, auditable and source-grounded, while keeping a person in charge when the numbers do not reconcile?

Built independently for MGT 409 from public Chapter 11 filings only. No competition research, team material or assumptions are used, and the app was not used for any competition submission.

The problem

One assumption moves the fulcrum

Wolfspeed, filed High case vs plant & equipment at the Low-case 13.7% of book; other High-case assumptions and costs held fixed. Engine output from the real extraction.

  • Net distributable value: $2.76bn → $1.51bn
  • Fulcrum moves from the unsecured classes to the Senior Secured Notes (83.6%); a 5.3-point cut already moves it to the admin tier.
  • Structure matters too: one consolidated Enviva waterfall with the DIP ranked first gives the DIP lender about 46%; the debtor filed 18%.
  • Today: re-type a 9–17-page exhibit from a 217–460-page filing into Excel, rebuild the waterfall by hand.
Our solution

AI copies. Code computes. People decide when it doesn't reconcile.

Source-grounded extractionEvery number carries the exact table row it came from; code checks it is really printed there.
Deterministic waterfallAbsolute priority, pro rata within a class. No arithmetic in the model.
ReconciliationRecompute every filed scenario; RECONCILED only if it matches the debtor's own recoveries.
SensitivitySliders rerun the engine instantly, 0 tokens; the fulcrum is shown.
Human reviewNEEDS REVIEW is never hidden; corrections need a name and keep provenance.

vs a PDF chatbot: auditable row by row, identical numbers every run, and the filed recoveries act as an answer key that exposes a wrong structure. Octus, 9fin, Fitch's recovery tool and AlphaSense/Hebbia offer data, waterfalls or cited search; none of their public pages describes recomputing and reconciling a debtor's filed liquidation analysis.

Architecture

One agent, everything else code

FastAPI + one static page. Every run logs tokens and cost (usage_log.json), the text sent (audit_trail.json), the result and provenance (extractions/*.json).

Real demo

WW reconciles; Wolfspeed's fulcrum moves

Responsible failure

Enviva and Dean Foods: ⚠ NEEDS REVIEW

The tool says what it cannot verify instead of producing a confident, wrong recovery. A reviewer's corrections are logged, and still cannot force a reconciliation.

Tokenomics & safety

About a fifth of a cent per filing — measured

All 10 live extractions from output/usage_log.json (cyan = reconciled, amber = needs review).

$0.0020mean cost / run
7,478mean input tokens
2,440mean output tokens
  • Exhibit only: ~6K tokens instead of a ~159K-token filing (WW).
  • 20 runs/user/month ≈ $0.04; 10,000 users ≈ $410/month in model cost.
  • Planted hidden + visible instruction: hidden withheld, visible flagged, still 108/108.
  • Fabricated number → one targeted retry → corrected; caps of 4 requests / 80K tokens; rate limit.
Impact — what was actually measured

Accurate where verifiable, honest where not

7/7live runs with every one of 764 scored fields correct (5 repeats on WW, 2 on Wolfspeed)
12–22 smodel time per filing; stress tests instant
≈ 4 minfresh clone → reconciled live run (graders' .env layout)
  • Dean Foods live test (author's run): 11 claim classes extracted in 22 s of model time for $0.0021; correctly flagged NEEDS REVIEW.
  • Not measured: time saved versus Excel, or a user's opinion. An earlier user trial was reported but has no artifacts, so no claim is made from it.
Conclusion

Reproducible numbers, visible assumptions, human judgment

  • Source-grounded extraction + deterministic reconciliation turns a fragile spreadsheet exercise into an auditable one.
  • Sensitivity is explicit: the fulcrum is always on screen.
  • When structure is beyond the engine, a person decides — by design.
